Review of the names of the birds and give general information about the birds

blocks.text: The guide reviews with the child the name of the birds in the chart and their representative on the third row – the parrot.
The guide reinforces that these 8 groups are just examples of the many groups
f birds that exist.
The names of the orders of birds end with –formes.
The guide says that the bones of the birds are hollow, which makes them light for flying.

The guide says that the birds have all of them wings and the wings are coloured with feathers. The birds are warm blooded so they can regulate their body temperature allowing them to be active when it is cold. Warm blooded animals use a lot of energy and the feathers are used for insulation and/or flying.

The guide says that the reptiles have eggs with soft shells but the birds have eggs with hard shells. Reptiles lay eggs and leave them in warm places, in contrast the birds have to warm their eggs with their bodies.
The birds have an organ called “the crop” that helps them to grind the seeds they eat.

children.title: Presentation of the ostrich and introduction of the concept: struthianiformes

blocks.text: The guide says that the birds and the mammals lived at the same time this is why there is no age of the birds.

The guide says that the ostrich is the largest living bird, they don’t have big wings but have powerful legs. The bones of the ostrich are heavy, and their feet have 2 toes. Because the ostrich is a large and heavy bird the ostrich egg has a very tough shell.
The guide talks about the feathers or plumage which for the male are black and white and for the female is brown. The ostriches have eyelashes. The name
f the group comes from old name in Greek for ostrich: struthian with the
ending –formes giving us struthianiformis.
The guide says that in the group with the ostrich some scientists include the emu and the kiwi.

children.title: Presentation of the duck and introduction of the concept: anseriformes

blocks.text: The guide says that the ducks can use all the elements: land, water and air. Some of the species of ducks can migrate long distances.
The guide says the name of the group of the ducks comes from the Latin name for geese: anseri with the ending –formes giving us anseriformes.

children.title: Presentation of the stork and introduction of the concept: ciconiiformes

blocks.text: The guide says that the group of the storks includes the flamingos. The legs of the stork are stilt like. This kind of legs are good for muddy/marshy terrains. The long beaks that they have are called bills and are excellent for finding food in the water.
The guide says the name of the group of the storks comes from the Latin name for stork: ciconia with the ending –formes giving us ciconiiformes.

children.title: Presentation of the rooster and introduction of the concept: galliformes

blocks.text: The guide says that the group of the roosters includes the chicken and all the gain birds (pheasant, turkey). They have strong feet for scratching in the grounds. Their beaks are short but strong. The group represented by the roosters is the most extended on earth because of being a food source for the humans.
The guide says the name of the group of the roosters comes from the Latin name for rooster: Gallus with the ending –formes giving us galliformes

children.title: Presentation of the pigeon and introduction of the concept: columbiformes

blocks.text: The guide says that the group of the pigeons includes the doves. The pigeons have 4 toes. The birds have a syrinx which is used for singing in same fashion as the humans can use the larynges.
The guide says the name of the group of the pigeons comes from the Latin name for pigeon like: Columbi with the ending –formes giving us columbiformes

children.title: Presentation of the sparrow and introduction of the concept: passeriformes

blocks.text: The guide says that the group of the sparrow is the largest bird group including more than half of the birds. The birds in this group can perch (sit on a branch), can sing beautiful songs but all of them are named for the sparrow.
The guide says the name of the group of the sparrows comes from the Latin name for sparrow like: passeri with the ending –formes giving us passeriformes

children.title: Presentation of the woodpecker and introduction of the concept: piciformes

blocks.text: The guide says that the woodpecker pecks to make their nest and to find food (grubs). Their feet have 4 toes, 2 in the front and 2 in the back.
The guide says the name of the group of the woodpecker comes from the Latin name for woodpeckers: Picus with the ending –formes giving us piciformes

children.title: Presentation of the eagle and introduction of the concept: falconiformes

blocks.text: The guide says that the eagles have very strong toes called talons, they have very good eyesight and they can hunt on the wing. The humans always admired the eagles and used their image to represent souvergnity.

children.title: Presentation of the platypus and introduction of the concept: monotreme

blocks.text: The guide says that the platypus lives in Australia, lives in water and on the land. His body is covered with fur and for the mouth it has a duck kind of bill. The platypus lays eggs but feeds the young ones with milk.
The guide talks about the platypus remembers us of the first mammals that were the oviparous mammals.
The guide says the name of the group of the platypus is named for the only one
pening at the back or monotreme and comes from the Latin name
mono+treme for one opening.

children.title: Presentation of the kangaroo and introduction of the concept: marsupials

blocks.text: The guide says that the kangaroo lives in Australia and the most special feature it is the pouch. All the mammals in Australia at the beginning has pouches.
The guide says the group of the kangaroo is named for the pouches: marsupials. The name comes from the Latin name marsupium for the pouch.

children.title: Presentation of the anteater and introduction of the concept: edentates

blocks.text: The guide says that the anteater have just a few teeth and instead of many teeth have a sticky tongue.
The guide says the group of the anteater is named for the lack of teeth: edentates. The name comes from the Latin name edentate for the missing teeth.

children.title: Presentation of the beaver and introduction of the concept: rodents

blocks.text: The guide says that the beavers have very strong teeth at the front that keep growing, for this reason the beaver has to gnaw.
The guide says that there are other animals in this group: rabbits, chipmunks, etc.
The guide says the group of the beaver is named for the continuous gnawing: rodents. The name comes from the Latin name rodere for the gnawing.

children.title: Presentation of the zebra and introduction of the concept: ungulates

blocks.text: The guide says that the zebras live in groups called heard and they remember us of the horse. The zebras are very good runners and they are running on their “toe nails” or hoofs.
The guide says that there are other animals in this group: horses, goats, giraffes, cows, etc.
The guide says the group of the zebras is named for the hoofs: ungulates. The name comes from the Latin name unguis for the nail.

children.title: Presentation of the mole and introduction of the concept: insectivore

blocks.text: The guide says that the moles live in the underground and feed themselves with worms and grubs. They have poor eyesight and the fur can run in both ways which helps them to move in the tunnels.
The guide says the group of the moles is named for their appetite for insects: insectivore. The name comes from the Latin name insect+vore for insect eater.

children.title: Presentation of the whale and introduction of the concept: cetaceans

blocks.text: The guide says that the whales live only into the water and they can’t survive
ut of the water. The front limbs of whales are called flippers, they have back
limbs but are not very visible. The end of the tale is called fluke. The whale fat it is called: whale blubber.

The guide talks about the fact that the whale give birth to their babies in the water. In the group of the whale there are the dolphins and porpoises. The two groups of whales are baleen (whales that have a grid instead of teeth) and toothed.
The guide says the group of the whale is named from their names in Greek and Latin: ketos and cetos: cetaceans.

children.title: Presentation of the seal and introduction of the concept: pinnipeds

blocks.text: The guide says that the seals have bodies that are good for moving in the water. The seals have their bodies covered in fur. The seals have 2 pairs of limbs: flippers and fin like limbs in the back.
The guide says the group of the moles is named for their fin like back limbs: pinnipeds. The name comes from the Latin name pinna+peds for wings/fin footed.

children.title: Presentation of the lion and introduction of the concept: carnivores

blocks.text: The guide says that the lions eat only meat. They are great hunters with well- developed teeth: canines.
The guide says the group of the lions is named for their meat appetite: carnivores. The name comes from the Latin name carni+vore for meat eater.

children.title: Presentation of the bat and introduction of the concept: chiropterans

blocks.text: The guide says that the bats eat insects and are the only winged mammals. Their wings are in fact fingers with skin in between, so we could think of them as big hands. Bats have fur as their mammals.
The guide says the group of the bats is named for their hand - wings: chiropteran. The name comes from the Latin words cheir+pteran for hand wings.

children.title: Presentation of the dugong/sea cow and introduction of the concept: sirenions

blocks.text: The guide says that the dugongs live completely into water: in rivers, estuaries
r coastal areas (fresh water and brackish water (fresh and salty water). The
dugong have well developed limbs. The front limbs are called flipper. The dugongs are called the mermaids.
The guide says the group of the dugong is named for their mermaid like appearance: sirenions. The name comes from the Latin word siren for mermaids.

children.title: Presentation of the gibbon and introduction of the concept: primates

blocks.text: The guide says that the gibbons have no tails. The monkeys and the apes were the last ones to appear and are found at the end of the timeline of life.

The guide talks about the fact that the primates have a pair of limbs that we can regard as hands with 5 toes on each limb, have opposable thumbs and forward facing eyes. Most of the primates can keep learning all their life as
pposed to the other mammals that learn only at a very young age. This
capacity it is called neoteny.
The guide says the group of the gibbon is named for their appearance close to the humans: primates. The name comes from the Latin word primus for first.

Cyclostomata is a group of agnathans that comprises the living jawless fishes: the lampreys and hagfishes. Both groups have jawless mouths with horny epidermal structures that function as teeth, and branchial arches that are internally positioned instead of external as in jawed fishes. The name Cyclostomata means "round mouths".
Hagfish, the class Myxini (also known as Hyperotreti), are eel-shaped, slime-producing marine fish (occasionally called slime eels). They are the
nly known living animals that have a skull but no vertebral column,

although hagfish do have rudimentary vertebrae. Along with lampreys, hagfish are jawless; they are the sister group to jawed vertebrates, and living hagfish remain similar to hagfish from around 300 million years ago.

children.title: The Great River

blocks.text: The fable can be presented towards the end of the first cycle. The Great River it is different from the other fables as it doesn’t follow a natural sequence. If the first three fables are presenting the nature, the next ones pass to the humans and with this fable we are back to nature.

This fable stands apart because it has to do with the human body. The story is told with the chart which is highly impressionistic and it is used only as a mathematical aid. The aim is to arouse interest in the human body.

The fable has been reviewed and firstly published by Baiba Krumins Grazzini. There were three versions of the story and this one it is based on the 1961-1962 that Mario Montessori gave to the Bergamo staff in the first course.
Chart of the “Great River”

children.title: Presentation of the “Story of The Great River”
Show the chart and tell the story

blocks.text: Today, I would like to tell you another story, a strange story, a really strange story. Indeed, it does seem the most fantastic fable. It’s a “once upon a time” story; but strangely enough, it’s also a “right now” story. If I say once upon a time, how old is the story? As old as the Earth? No, but it’s a story that is as old as human beings. So it’s a fable born with human beings and it’s about human beings, which is why it’s true right now. So let’s listen to the story.

I know of a marvellous nation, a marvellous country, where the inhabitants are more numerous than all those populating our planet. Do you know how many people there are living on the Earth at the moment? More than 7 billion! Well, this marvellous country has many, many more inhabitants than that. How extraordinary! A country, which has more inhabitants than the whole of our planet Earth. But then, this is a strange story about a strange country.
The inhabitants that make up this marvellous nation are organized into all sorts
f groups and regions, all of which are very important. But for us, most important
f all, is the Great River that runs throughout the whole of the country,
throughout the whole of the nation.

The Great River has many, many branches: larger branches like tributaries, smaller streams, and channels that become smaller and smaller and smaller so that they can reach every zone of the country. All sorts of traffic goes up and down the Great River, up and down the tributaries, up and down all the
branches that become smaller and smaller; so that the traffic reaches every village, every field, every single inhabitant.

Most of the inhabitants of this country live hidden away from sight and so the Great River, which links all of them, has to flow in secret. A secret river? Hidden inhabitants? Well, what can you expect? This is a strange story about a strange country with a strange river and strange inhabitants…

The inhabitants are very strange because they work all the time. All the time! It’s as though they only live to work, as though they live only for the purpose of working. And they only work at the task, at the job, that’s been assigned to them. We said there were different groups, and each group works at only one particular task. So the inhabitants are highly specialized. These inhabitants even transform their bodies according to the particular task they have to do. They are not like us. We have all sorts of special instruments to help us; their special instrument is their body.

They work all the time, day and night, night and day. They never rest, they never strike. They don’t just work to live, it would be far truer to say that they live to work. Each group is totally dedicated to, and completely focused on its special task. They work unconsciously but it’s almost as though they know that the work they do is essential for the good of the whole country.

As we said, most of the inhabitants are hidden from sight, and the Great River flows in secret and links up all the inhabitants through innumerable streams and channels. (When you think of the Great River you have to think of the whole river system.)

From the Great River the different groups of workers can take whatever they need, because the Great River provides for everything they need. They, in turn, put back into the river whatever they produce that they don’t need for themselves. In this way, the products of the work of the inhabitants are distributed throughout the nation and so the Great River makes life possible for all the inhabitants of the country. The river, then, is a great means of communication. But the river does something else as well: not only does it carry whatever is needed to all the inhabitants; the river also carries away all the waste or garbage. By bringing whatever is needed and by taking away all the waste, the river ensures that the nation remains healthy. This nation is a truly marvellous nation: a nation wanted by God, a nation where all is harmony and constant work.

We have understood that these inhabitants work all the time, but what about harmony? Who commands in this nation? Who makes up the government? Well, it’s also a strange government; for one thing, it hasn’t changed in hundreds of thousands of years. But then, this is a strange country with a strange river and strange inhabitants and so perhaps we should expect a strange government! The government never changes, but the inhabitants are completely obedient. They work all the time. If they didn’t work all the time, the nation would perish. And so they work all their lives and when they die, they just slip away into the river. There are no tears, no mourning, no ceremonies;

everyone just keeps on working because that is what is important for the nation. The inhabitants don’t think about why they exist, don’t think about why they are working, they just work and that’s that. They are all the same when it comes to working: they all work equally hard and they are all equally willing to be
bedient. They are obedient right up until they die. Therefore this nation is

really not like the nations we know: the inhabitants of this nation can’t make their voices heard and they don’t get to vote. They never get to vote, but they always obey the government. The government is a part of the country yet somewhat isolated, and the ones that form the government always keep their
wn job. They don’t take turns to do different jobs; they too are specialized.

We could compare the place where the government is found, to a strong and fortified castle. And the river that feeds the workers, that keeps the country clean, that defends and brings life to the entire nation, that same river flows through the fortified castle.

Let us suppose that the beings governing from this strange castle constitute the presidency, then the zones into which the country is divided we can think of as departments. The castle rules over all the departments. What are the departments? There is a department of nutrition, department of air, department of defense and department of the boundaries of the nation, department of sensations, department of sanitation or purification, and also the department of transport. And what is that department? It’s the Great River.

Each department is an entity into itself, but each one is united with the others. How is this done, how is this unification achieved? Partly by the Great River and partly in another way. We said there is a department of sensations and all sensations are immediately reported to the castle where the government lives. The government then immediately sends out commands to the right places so that appropriate action can be taken. All of this is done with incredible speed and precision. Therefore each part of the nation has a special, fast means of communication with that strange castle. Consequently, even though the departments are separate, they are continually in contact with one another both by way of the Great River and through other special channels of communication.

Let’s come back to our Great River. We have already said it’s essential to the health of the nation. We have said that it runs both in great branches and tiny channels so that it can reach the farthest-flung boundaries of the nation. Do you know where this river that flows in secret can be found? Can you guess where you can find this strange nation? Would you like to know the name of the Great River that flows through this nation?

That strange and marvellous country where all the inhabitants work and live in harmony is the human body. The name of the Great River that runs through the body is blood: blood that flows and transports, blood that feeds, blood that cleans, defends and gives life to the country and its inhabitants, that keeps the inhabitants healthy. Who are the inhabitants? The cells in our body: that’s why we can say there are more of them then there are inhabitants in the whole world.

Can you feel the Great River that is flowing through each one of us right now? Can you feel its pulse? Do you see the strange nation, this strange country? The inhabitants are in each of us; the Great River flows through all of us. It flows throughout the body so that every single part is reached. The smallest parts from which our bodies are formed are the cells: a cell is very tiny, so tiny we can’t see it with the naked eye. Yet the Great River reaches every single cell, and all the cells together work unconsciously to keep the body alive. The human body is a marvelous and divine work of creation, where all is unconscious, untiring, constant, work; where all is perfect harmony. [Show the chart]

And here we have a chart for the Great River. We said the inhabitants of the country, the nation, of the Great River are the cells. The Great River itself is the blood, and the blood is carried through a system of vessels. The cells take from the Great River what they need and the put back into the Great River what they don’t need. The work of the Great River has to do with transport, and so here we have the department of transportation. All of the cells have their own special work to do. Here is the castle where we find the cells that govern. What do we find inside our skull? It’s somewhat separated but not isolated. So these cells can govern the body, they are not completely cut off. Then we have a windmill, the department of nutrition. It stands for all the specialized cells in the body that are involved in providing the food. The process starts when we put food into our mouth, but that food must reach the cells in a suitable form. We can see that represented here by the windmill and

a man carrying sacks. All sorts of specialized cells work together so that we can be nourished. (A windmill gives the idea of cereal, of wheat, of bread, and consequently the associated idea of nutrition.)

We heard about the department of air. That has to do with breathing and ensuring that each cell gets the oxygen it needs. This work is represented here by a man with bellows. The lungs are involved, the nose, the mouth; and the blood carries the oxygen to every cell. Here is the department of defense, we can see soldiers. They represent cells specialized in defending our body (white blood cells). These special cells protect us against invaders. Here is the department of sensations, we see a nose, a hand, an eye, an ear, a tongue. Each of these permits us to receive, to perceive, sensations: sensations to do with smelling, touching, seeing, hearing, and tasting. All the information received through these senses is conveyed to the government in the castle, which then sends out the commands to say what action has to be taken. All
f this takes place with incredible rapidity and precision. In this way, the
government is in continual and constant communication with the rest of the body.
Would you like to find out more about the human body?
